name: Morocco
headline: Political stability as a competitive advantage.
summary: Morocco has turned an ancient monarchy into an industrial platform oriented toward Europe and Africa. Its assets are stability, infrastructure, and renewables; its constraints remain youth unemployment, dependence on imported energy, and the Western Sahara conflict.

history.title: French protectorate
history.text: The Treaty of Fez places most of Morocco under a French protectorate, with a Spanish zone in the north. Modern administration and infrastructure develop.

history.title: Independence
history.text: Sultan Mohammed V becomes king. Morocco keeps a strong monarchy that guarantees national unity and the balance between tribes and cities.

history.title: The Green March
history.text: 350,000 Moroccans cross into Western Sahara. The territory becomes a national cause, a source of cohesion but also of lasting conflict with Algeria.

history.title: The reign of Mohammed VI
history.text: The new king modernizes the economy, launches major works, and gradually opens society while keeping the palace primacy.

history.title: Constitutional reform
history.text: In the wake of the Arab Spring, a new Constitution strengthens Parliament and the courts, without challenging the king's central role.

history.title: World Cup semi-final
history.text: The Atlas Lions reach the World Cup semi-finals in Qatar. Morocco's image and soft power change scale.

history.title: Year of football and the 2030 horizon
history.text: The 2025 Africa Cup of Nations and the 2030 World Cup, co-hosted with Spain and Portugal, accelerate investment in transport and energy.

institutions.executive: King as head of state and religious leader; Prime Minister from Parliament
institutions.legislature: Bicameral Parliament: House of Representatives and House of Councillors
institutions.central_bank: Bank Al-Maghrib, independent in conducting monetary policy
institutions.currency: Moroccan dirham (MAD), a managed float regime
institutions.law: Civil law based on French law; Muslim law for personal status
institutions.fact: Morocco was the first African country to sign a full free-trade agreement with the United States.

allies.name: France
allies.note: Leading economic and cultural partner, despite occasional tensions.

allies.name: United States
allies.note: Free-trade agreement and recognition of the Sahara autonomy plan.

rivals.name: Algeria
rivals.note: Closed borders, the Sahara dispute, and a race for regional influence.

dependencies.name: European Union
dependencies.note: Main outlet for autos, agro-industry, and textiles.

dependencies.name: Imported energy
dependencies.note: The country imports most of its hydrocarbons.

dependencies.name: Tourism and remittances
dependencies.note: Migrant transfers and tourism support the balance of payments.

gdp_growth.note: Growth is supported by industry, tourism, and football-related investment, but remains vulnerable to drought.

inflation.note: Inflation is back within the comfort zone. Lower food prices and the dirham's stability helped.

debt_gdp.note: Debt remains manageable, but the deficit and financing needs limit fiscal room.

policy_rate.note: The central bank cut its rate to support investment. The real rate remains positive but moderate.

unemployment.note: Unemployment is high, especially among youth and graduates. It is the main social weakness of the Moroccan model.

reserves.note: Reserves cover about five months of imports. That is decent, but less than Gulf standards.

rating.note: The rating has moved into the high speculative category. The reformist path and European anchoring support the outlook.

cds.note: The market prices moderate risk. Morocco borrows more expensively than Spain, but less than the more fragile African frontier countries.

equity_index.note: The index benefits from banks, real estate, and enthusiasm for World Cup-linked stocks.

currency.name: Moroccan dirham
currency.note: The dirham is managed within a band. Nominal stability is an advantage for European investors.

strengths: A hub position for industry and logistics between Europe and Africa.
risks: High youth unemployment and regional inequalities.
Dependence on energy imports and rainfall.
The Western Sahara conflict and frozen relations with Algeria.
opportunities: Electric autos and batteries thanks to agreements with Europe.
The 2030 World Cup and infrastructure modernization.

quiz.question: Why was the Green March of 1975 so formative for Morocco?
quiz.explanation: The Green March mobilized the population to claim the Western Sahara. The territory remains at the core of foreign policy and of the conflict with Algeria.
